label: SQP-style
stem: If a chart shows that a figure rose from 48% to 60%, the correct way to describe the change is
model_answer: **(b)** Percentage figures change in percentage points; 'by 12' or 'by 60%' is wrong.

label: SQP-style
stem: A survey finds that students who use screens late sleep less. Which conclusion does the data SUPPORT?
options: Screens cause poor sleep in all teenagers
There is a link between late screen use and shorter sleep among the students surveyed
Students who sleep less are lazy
Banning phones will make students sleep eight hours
model_answer: **(b)** A survey shows correlation within its sample, not cause or a guaranteed remedy.

label: SQP-style
stem: Read the practice passage 'Screen Time and Sleep: A School Survey' in the Read tab of this chapter, including its table, and answer the questions that follow. Allow 13 minutes.
hint: Read the table first: four classes, three measures, units (hours/day, hours/night, %). Mark the extremes: screen 2.4→4.6, sleep 8.1→6.4, late-night 18→64. Then the items.

parts.stem: How many students took part in the survey, and how were they distributed?
parts.model_answer: 400 students of Classes 9 to 12, 100 from each class.

parts.stem: Which class recorded the highest average screen time, and what was it?
By how many hours did average sleep fall between Class 9 and Class 12?
Between which two classes was the change in screen time the sharpest? Support with figures.
parts.model_answer: Between Classes 10 and 11: screen time rose by 1.1 hours (3.1 to 4.2), more than any other step.

parts.stem: The share of students using a screen after 11 p.m. rose from Class 9 to Class 12 by (A) 46% (B) 46 percentage points (C) 64 percentage points (D) 18 percentage points
parts.model_answer: (B) 18% to 64% is a rise of 46 percentage points.

parts.stem: What explanation does the passage offer for the sharp change between Classes 10 and 11?
parts.model_answer: That is the year most students get their own smartphone and begin preparing for competitive examinations.

scheme.step: Own smartphone; start of competitive-exam preparation

parts.stem: State TRUE or FALSE: Most late-night screen use among senior students was for study.
parts.model_answer: FALSE — study-related use was less than a quarter; messaging and short videos were most common.

parts.stem: Which word in paragraph 5 means 'suggested as a course of action'?
What did the surveying students conclude, and what caution did they add? (about 40 words)
parts.model_answer: They concluded that screen use in their school rises with age and that heavier screen users sleep less. They cautioned that a survey cannot prove that one causes the other, since older students also carry a heavier study load; they therefore asked for a repeat survey in March.

scheme.step: Conclusion: screen use rises with age; heavier users sleep less
Caution: correlation not cause; heavier study load; repeat survey
